summary: Agent 0.35.0 (ADR-0092): the RAM need the agent checks before releasing its held OpenAI-compatible server is now the larger of the peak working set of the server's process tree and the RAM released when a hold stops it, plus 10 %, growing only while the start configuration stays the same; previously the peak commit. Traced: router upstream-release order -> upstreamHold.apply -> ramBlock (the only RAM gate, ADR-0035) -> Supervisor.Release; sampler upstreamHold.sample/observeRun -> Supervisor.childMemory -> procTree.pids (job object) -> procMemory (K32GetProcessMemoryInfo, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, unchanged access right); hold path -> releasedSince (memoryFact) -> endRun -> saveUpstreamMemo (atomic write in the identity folder, unchanged). No new route, input from the network, privilege, file location or dependency. The gate becomes less strict by design (52.3 GiB commit -> resident need); the review checked that it does not undercount: the release measure covers driver-held pages outside the working set, the need never drops within a configuration, and a 10 % margin covers sampling gaps. upstream.json gains a 64-bit fingerprint of the child's command, folder, arguments and environment; the file lives in the agent's identity folder next to its private key, so it opens no new path to environment values.

findings.evidence: Replacing commit with a resident measure could undercount the RAM a start takes (the gate exists because a start at 98 % RAM was followed by a bluescreen): pages pinned for the GPU and trimmed from the working set, or allocated by the graphics kernel, are in no per-process counter; and resident memory grows over hours, so a short run (the router often holds the server seconds after it answers) would have lowered a last-run peak.
findings.resolution: The need also takes the RAM released when the server's tree ends (read before the stop, right after it and after two seconds, before the standby starts), never drops while the start configuration is the same, and carries a 10 % margin. Tests: TestHoldLearnsWithoutSample (release larger than the working set sets the need), TestSampleLearnsUpstream (commit ignored, a shorter run does not lower the need), TestNeedRelearned, TestChildConfig, TestProcMemory (real call: committed-only memory is not resident).

tests.command: Node check: one run of the server on a Windows node with agent 0.35.0, then compare upstream.json with the working-set peak and the RAM released at the stop
tests.evidence: Needs the maintainer's rollout of agent 0.35.0; the PR describes the check.

limitations: On the first start of agent 0.35.0 a need stored by an older agent (commit) is discarded, and after a change of the server's start configuration the need is learned again; until the next run is measured, a release has no RAM check, as on the first start since ADR-0037. A first short run learns less than a long one until a longer run raised it.

The release measure is read from system-wide available RAM and is blurred by other programs that change their memory in the same seconds; a drop (a game starting) is covered by the resident peak, a rise can only overstate.

How the GPU driver accounts pinned host memory on the node was not measured directly; the server was stopped during the probe. The node check in the PR compares released_bytes with peak_resident_bytes to show it.
